subject.title: feat(google-meet): retain the full caption transcript per session (#103387)

question: Should Google Meet ship a runtime-memory-only 2000-line transcript API across gateway, tool, and CLI, or should public transcript retrieval wait for a persisted SQLite-backed lifecycle?
rationale: The implementation adds a new user-facing retrieval contract whose retention lifetime, fixed cap, eviction behavior, and restart loss require product intent beyond the mechanical bounded-state fix.

options.title: Approve bounded runtime API
options.body: Ship the additive runtime-memory API after bounding all transcript state and obtaining live caption proof, with the documented restart and eviction semantics.

options.title: Require SQLite persistence
options.body: Pause this PR and define a plugin-owned persisted transcript lifecycle before exposing the public retrieval surfaces.

options.title: Keep status-only behavior
options.body: Decline the new transcript API and retain only the existing recent caption health fields.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded runtime API
recommendation.body: Ship the additive runtime-memory API after bounding all transcript state and obtaining live caption proof, with the documented restart and eviction semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged history identifies this person as the original Google Meet and caption-health owner and the most recent contributor to session ownership semantics.
